normalized.governing_thought: Yes, raise prices in 2027, but only for mid-market and enterprise. Hold SMB, test it, and fix the promotion cohort with onboarding, not price
executive_summary: Churn is rising in one place. About 90% of the SMB rise (2.0% → 3.1% a month) comes from the 2,100 customers who joined on the 2025 half-price promotion. Other SMB customers moved from 2.0% to 2.1%.
The promotion cohort is an onboarding problem. Only 41% got started properly (72% for other cohorts), and most leavers went within two months of the discount ending.
Mid-market and enterprise can take an increase. Their NRR is 112% and 118%, a +10% list test had no significant effect on conversion, and Inkwell is absent above 200 seats.
SMB is the open question. Inkwell sells at $9 against our $15. A 12% SMB increase adds about $1.2M if customers react as they did in 2023, and nothing if they react twice as strongly.
The CFO's $10.3M is $7.6M before any churn response, because only part of the ARR renews in 2027 and enterprise increases are capped.
Mid-market: +10% list price at renewal (the tested level).
Enterprise: up to the 7% cap where contracts cap increases; up to +10% elsewhere.
SMB: hold $15 in H1 and split-test +8% in Q1. Extend it to H2 renewals only if churn holds.
Promotion cohort: no increase. Run an onboarding programme aimed at returning it to normal SMB churn.
$4.3M ARR from price, plus up to $0.7M if the SMB test passes; ~114% overall NRR (target above 100%); +14.2% growth from existing customers. About $0.6M of new-customer ARR reaches 15%
Trade-off: on paper this is $0.8–2.0M less 2027 ARR than the CFO's plan. In return, we avoid betting the 5,900-customer SMB base on a reaction we have not measured.

claims.claim: If the promotion cohort churned like other SMB customers, SMB churn would be 2.1%, not 3.1%. About 1.0 of the 1.1-point rise is the cohort.

72% of customers in other cohorts did the same
~3× higher churn for SMB customers who send fewer than five documents in month one

So what: the CFO is right that this is mostly an onboarding problem. It also means this cohort will not absorb a further increase in 2027.

slides.title: SMB is now exposed on price. A 12% increase pays off only if customers react less than twice as strongly as they did in 2023, and we cannot yet tell

claims.claim: SMB is now exposed on price.
evidence: List price per user per month: Inkwell Starter $9 (launched Oct 2025); Palisade SMB $15 today; Palisade SMB +12% $16.80 CFO proposal; Inkwell Pro $24; Palisade Business $29
Win rate vs Inkwell in SMB: 51% → 38% (H1 2025 → H1 2026).

claims.claim: A 12% increase pays off only if customers react less than twice as strongly as they did in 2023.
evidence: Net 2027 ARR effect of +12% on all SMB: No reaction +$2.5M; As in 2023 +$1.2M; 2× the 2023 reaction ≈ $0.0M; 3× the 2023 reaction −$1.3M

Gross gain is 12% × $21.0M = $2.5M. The 2023 response, scaled to 12%, means +0.75 pts of churn for six months and +0.15 pts after, losing about 5.4% of SMB customers. Break-even is about twice the 2023 reaction.
2023 precedent: +8% at renewal lifted SMB churn from 1.8% to 2.3% for six months, then it settled at 1.9%. That was before Inkwell existed.

claims.claim: The win-rate drop makes that plausible but not proven.
evidence: Pointing the other way: regular SMB churners citing price are flat (18% vs 19%).

slides.title: Mid-market and enterprise show pricing power. A 10% increase breaks even only if mid-market churn roughly doubles

claims.claim: Retention is strong
evidence: Net revenue retention: 112% mid-market, 118% enterprise
Monthly logo churn: 0.8% mid-market, 0.2% enterprise

claims.claim: Price was tested
evidence: 2024: +10% list price for new mid-market sign-ups
Conversion 23.1% vs 23.6% for the control group, not statistically significant

evidence: Inkwell not seen in mid-market or enterprise deals above 200 seats
Customers stay for integrations and audit trail (advisory board, 2026)

claims.claim: A 10% increase breaks even only if mid-market churn roughly doubles
evidence: Mid-market monthly logo churn: H1 2025 0.6%; H1 2026 0.8%; Proposed tripwire 1.2%; Break-even ~1.6%
Break-even: +10% on renewing ARR is lost if an extra 9.1% of renewing customers leave within the year (0.10 ÷ 1.10). That is about +0.8 pts a month on top of today's 0.8%.

claims.claim: Why +10%, not the CFO's 12%
evidence: 10% is the level we tested. 12% on existing customers is untested.
The test covered new sign-ups. Renewing customers may react differently, so watch Q1 renewals.
Mid-market churn is up 0.2 pts, and accounts of 200 seats or fewer may meet Inkwell.
Cost of the caution: $0.7M of 2027 ARR.

slides.title: The CFO's $10.3M assumes all ARR reprices in 2027. The realistic figure is $7.6M before any churn response, and $5.0–6.3M after it

Assumes 2027 enterprise renewals carry the same 60% capped share as the whole enterprise book, and 85% of mid-market ARR renews in 2027 (per the pack). The SMB response uses the 2023 precedent scaled to 12%. Mid-market and enterprise reactions are not modelled.

slides.title: How the main figures were calculated

claims.claim: CFO headline
evidence: 12% × $86.0M = $10.3M. This assumes every dollar of ARR reprices in 2027 at the full 12%.

claims.claim: CFO before churn response
evidence: SMB 12% × $21.0M = $2.52M; mid-market 12% × 85% × $41.0M = $4.18M; enterprise renewing $9.6M (40% of $24.0M): 60% capped at 7% = $0.40M, plus 40% at 12% = $0.46M. Total $7.57M.

claims.claim: SMB churn response
evidence: 2023: +8% gave +0.5 pts for six months, then +0.1 pts. Scaled linearly to 12%: +0.75 pts × 6 months + 0.15 pts × 6 months = 5.4% of customers lost, × $23.5M repriced ARR = $1.27M (×2 = $2.54M).

claims.claim: Recommended price ARR
evidence: Mid-market 10% × $34.85M = $3.49M. Enterprise: $5.76M capped at 7% = $0.40M, plus $3.84M at 10% = $0.38M. Total $4.27M.

claims.claim: SMB H2 option
evidence: +8% on roughly half of regular SMB ARR (renewing in H2): 8% × 50% × $16.6M ≈ $0.66M. Regular SMB ARR = $21.0M − $4.4M cohort.

claims.claim: Existing-customer bridge
Break-evens
evidence: Gain p is cancelled when the share of customers lost in the year reaches p ÷ (1 + p). Mid-market at 10%: 9.1% a year ≈ +0.8 pts a month. SMB at 8%: 7.4% ≈ +0.6 pts. SMB at 12%: 10.7%, about twice the 2023 response.

claims.claim: Promotion-cohort value
evidence: 12-month retention at 4.9% a month = 55%; at 2.1% = 78%. Difference × $4.4M ≈ $1.0M.

claims.claim: SMB test size
evidence: About 1,900 customers per arm for three months at a 2.1% base rate gives a standard error of about 0.27 pts on the difference. A 0.6-pt reaction is about 2.2 standard errors (detectable); a 0.3-pt reaction is about 1.1 (not). This assumes most test customers renew within Q1, which needs monthly plans; fewer renewals means a weaker test.

slides.title: The board churn figure cannot be reproduced. This page also lists the choices made where the briefing pack was silent

claims.claim: None of the obvious definitions gives 1.4% → 2.3%. Until Finance defines the figure, it should not be used for this decision.
evidence: H1 2025 → H1 2026: Board dashboard (undefined) 1.4% → 2.3%; Customer-weighted logo churn 1.7% → 2.6%; ARR-weighted logo churn 0.8% → 1.2%; SMB logo churn 2.0% → 3.1%
Weighted with mid-2026 customer counts and ARR from Table 1.

claims.claim: Choices made where the pack was silent
evidence: Mid-market increase set at 10%, the tested level, rather than 12%.
SMB test at +8%, the 2023 level, so the 2023 response is a usable benchmark.
Enterprise uncapped renewals at up to +10%, matching mid-market. Actual terms vary by contract.
2027 enterprise renewals assumed 60% capped, the same share as the whole enterprise book.
2027 NRR before price assumed equal to trailing 12-month NRR. The SMB figure (94%) includes the promotion cliff, so it is probably conservative.
Renewals spread evenly through the year, so about half of SMB ARR renews in H2.
Promotion-cohort churn (4.9%) is implied from blended and regular SMB rates, weighted by mid-2026 counts.
Not in the pack, so not modelled: new-customer bookings, gross margin, and the cost of the onboarding programme.

claims.claim: What would change the recommendation
evidence: SMB test shows little reaction → extend +8% to H2 SMB renewals (already in the rule).
Mid-market renewals react much more than the new-sign-up test suggested → pause at the tripwire.
New-customer bookings fall short of ~$0.6M → revisit the 12% mid-market option ($0.7M).

normalized.recommendation: Raise mid-market and enterprise prices at renewal, hold the SMB list price while we test it, and onboard the promotion cohort: Mid-market +10% list price at renewal from January 2027; Enterprise up to the 7% cap on capped contracts and up to +10% on uncapped renewals; SMB regular hold $15 in H1, split-test +8% on half of renewals in Q1 and apply +8% to H2 renewals if the test passes; SMB promotion cohort no increase in 2027, run an onboarding programme. Total +$4.3M of 2027 ARR from price, with up to +$1.7M of upside. We also recommend not repeating untargeted 50%-off promotions for new self-serve customers.

It reprices all 5,900 SMB incl. the promo cohort, uses an untested 12% on mid-market renewals, and mixes price with promo exits so churn cannot be read.

Not chosen yet. Adds about $1.2M if customers react as in 2023, nothing at 2× the reaction, −$1.3M at 3×; break-even is about twice the 2023 reaction and the win-rate drop makes that plausible but not proven. SMB held and tested at +8% instead.
Rejected: 10% is the tested level; 12% on existing customers is untested. Cost of the caution: $0.7M of 2027 ARR. Revisit if new-customer bookings fall short of ~$0.6M.

alternatives_considered.option: Price increase for the 2025 promotion cohort
alternatives_considered.treatment: Rejected: the cohort will not absorb a further increase in 2027; price would accelerate churn. Onboarding programme instead.
Rejected as target: halving 3.1% means 1.55%, below any level since 2023; realistic target is ~2.1% (cohort churns like regular SMB).

Using the board dashboard churn metric (1.4% → 2.3%)

normalized.extraction_notes: The deck came as plain text with no images, so there was nothing to transcribe from pictures. Chart values on slides 3, 5, 6, 7, 9 and 10 came out as loose label and number fragments. I paired them with their categories using the order they appear in, so these pairings are reconstructed, not explicit. On slide 2, the KPI figures ($4.3M, ~114%, +14.2%) were split from their labels, and I recombined each figure with its label. For the governing thought I used the slide 2 (executive summary) title. The slide 1 title is a shorter version of the same answer.
